walkthroughs.body_html:
Religious & Ethical Teachings about Medical Ethics — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religious & Ethical Teachings about Medical Ethics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religious & Ethical Teachings about Medical Ethics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Substance dualism means men and women are different.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
Tawhid is the Islamic word for the Trinity.
The absolute oneness and indivisibility of Allah — the most fundamental Islamic belief. Its opposite, shirk (associating partners with God), is the gravest sin.
